message.content:
I don’t have access to real‑time data, so I can’t tell you the exact current time right now.  
If you need the precise time in New York City, you can:

1. **Check your device’s clock** – most smartphones, computers, and smart‑home assistants automatically adjust for the local time zone.  
2. **Use an online time‑zone converter** – sites like [timeanddate.com](https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/) or the “World Clock” feature on Google give you the current time for any city.  
3. **Ask a voice assistant** – say “Hey Siri, what time is it in New York?” or “Alexa, what’s the time in New York?”

If you’re looking for a quick reference, New York City is in the Eastern Time Zone (UTC‑5 in standard time, UTC‑4 during daylight‑saving time). On June 2, 2026, daylight‑saving time is in effect, so the offset is UTC‑4. If you know the current UTC time, subtract four hours to get the local time in NYC.
